title: Ralph Fiennes Reunites With ‘Conclave’ Producer Tessa Ross & Studiocanal For Story Of Legendary Trainer Henry Cecil & Champion Horse Frankel
full_text: Skip to main content By Andreas Wiseman Andreas Wiseman Executive Editor, Film & International @AndreasWiseman More Stories By Andreas Renny Harlin To Direct Prison Rescue Thriller ‘Evac’ ‘Red Sonja’ Producer Christa Campbell Launches Film & TV Company XTA Media Ron Perlman Lines Up Hemingway Movie & Updates On ‘Sons Of Anarchy’ Spinoff ‘Legends’, That Third ‘Hellboy’ Film & Next Steps For His Asylm Studios View All October 15, 2026 7:02am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Ralph Fiennes, Henry Cecil, Frankel Lea Meienberg/Getty EXCLUSIVE : Three-time Oscar nominee Ralph Fiennes is reuniting with Conclave producer Tessa Ross and A Bigger Splash backer Studiocanal on Unbeaten , a biopic of legendary British horse racing trainer Henry Cecil and his most famous charge, Frankel. Fiennes will star as Cecil and serve as executive producer on the film, which is being lined up to shoot next year. The screenplay from Boardwalk Empire WGA nominee Bash Doran, the consulting producer on Beef , will be directed by BAFTA winner Nora Fingscheidt ( System Crasher ) with Tessa Ross producing for House Productions and Rory Aitken producing for Escapade Pictures. 42 will also produce. Pic has been developed with support from BBC Film and Conclave and The Zone Of Interest backer Access Entertainment. Related Stories News Ralph Fiennes, Colin Farrell & Wagner Moura Set For Comedy 'Art' From Director Fernando Meirelles & Screenwriter Christopher Hampton; 193 Launches For Cannes Market News Ralph Fiennes, Viggo Mortensen, Charlotte Rampling, Katherine Langford & More Set For István Szabó's 'Embers'; Filming Underway & First Looks Revealed With Embankment Aboard For Cannes Market Studiocanal is fully financing the film and will release theatrically in their territories of the UK, France, Germany, Italy, Poland, Benelux, Australia and New Zealand. Executive producers include Anna Marsh, Ron Halpern and Joe Naftalin for Studiocanal, as well as Fiennes and Doran. Studiocanal is handling worldwide sales. Watch on Deadline Cecil, knighted by the Queen in 2011, was one of horse racing’s most recognizable and celebrated global figures. A ten-time champion trainer in the UK, the undefeated Frankel was his most famous horse, winning ten Group 1 races. Many consider the horse to be the greatest European thoroughbred ever and a rival to U.S. champ Secretariat. The film will follow the late Cecil’s bittersweet final years as he triumphantly rebuilds his career and life after suffering personal heartbreak, tabloid scandal, health crises and falling out with the industry’s most powerful owner. The relationship with Frankel and rekindling with his third wife Jane McKeown were key to his return to the top of his sport. Tony Rushmer, author of The Triumph of Henry Cecil: The Authorised Biography , is a consultant on the film. Ralph Fiennes commented: “I knew nothing about the legendary Henry Cecil until I read Bash Doran’s screenplay. I was compelled and moved by it and by Henry’s story with the great horse Frankel. Henry was – and still is – a unique figure, complex and competitive in the very specific world of horse racing. I’m delighted to be reunited with Tessa Ross (producer) and to be working alongside Rory Aitken (producer) and Studiocanal. I’m particularly excited to be collaborating with Nora Fingscheidt. Her intensely immersive approach and desire for authenticity is inspiring. I was blown away by her film The Outrun .” The project marks the second collaboration between Berlin Silver Bear winner Fingscheidt and Euro studio Studiocanal following the UK release of BAFTA nominated The Outrun , starring Saoirse Ronan. Fiennes is repped by 42 Management and Production, CAA, and SOWDLLP. Fingscheidt is with Casarotto Ramsay & Associates, Ilene Feldman Management and Homebase. Doran is repped by UTA, Untitled and Schreck Rose. title: Disney+ And Hulu To Stream Pave Studios True-Crime Podcasts ‘Clues’ And ‘Mother Knows Murder’
full_text: Skip to main content By Dade Hayes Dade Hayes Business Editor @dadehayes More Stories By Dade Skydance Shares Tumble In Technical Adjustment As Inflation, Interest Rate Jitters Roil Markets; Apple Regains $5 Trillion Market Cap Candle In The Wind: 5-Year-Old Media Firm Faces New Questions After Hello Sunshine Exit ‘Elsinore’ And ‘La Bola Negra’ Continue Awards Momentum With Wins At Hamptons Film Festival View All October 15, 2026 7:01am Add us as a Google Preferred Source EXCLUSIVE: Disney+ and Hulu will stream Pave Studios true-crime video podcasts Clues and Mother Knows Murder in exclusive windows before they go into wide release. The two titles, which are part of Pave’s Crime House sub-brand, are the company’s first to be picked up by a major streaming platform. Seeing the growth of YouTube in the living room, Netflix, HBO Max, Peacock and lately Disney+ have been looking to add podcast programming, which is seen as a budget-friendly way to boost view time and engagement. Pave Studios was founded by Max Cutler, who previously founded Parcast and went on to become an executive at Spotify after the streaming giant acquired his company. Related Stories News British True Crime Producer Association Welcomes Non-UK Producers For First Time Including America's Gennie Studios, My Entertainment and Texas Crew Legal FBI Adds Ex-Bellum Entertainment CEO To Most Wanted Fraudsters List; Offering $150K Reward For Info On Fugitive Mary Carole McDonnell Clues , hosted by Kaelyn Moore, will premiere next Tuesday. Mother Knows Murder , hosted by The Rookie: Feds and Claws star Niecy Nash and her daughter, actress Dia Nash, will debut on November 9. Watch on Deadline New episodes of both series will premiere on Disney+ and Hulu one day before they become available on other podcast platforms. Clues , which won a Webby earlier this year, promises to take viewers and listeners “deep into the world of notorious crimes and forensic breakthroughs.” New podcast Mother Knows Murder sees the Nashes breaking down an actual case as they recline in bed. Moore, known as the host of Heart Starts Pounding and the newly premiered Last Trace with Kaelyn Moore said Clues “was developed with a streaming audience in mind from day one. Our goal was to create a show with the production quality and storytelling that would stand naturally alongside other premium content on a streamer like Disney+ and Hulu.” Cutler said the Disney streaming deal is “proof” of the audience-friendly, creator-led approach of Crime House. Disney is “the first of many places we expect these stories to go,” he added. “As streaming platforms increasingly look to add premium content from talented creators, Pave is well-positioned to be a content collaborator to these companies, and we are excited to be working with Disney to bring our shows to their streaming viewers.” Zendaya Set For Alex Garland’s Untitled Science Fiction Movie At A24 Key Takeaways Including ‘Baywatch’, YouTube, Skydance & Banijay UK Gov’t “Minded To Intervene” Over $2.1B Sky-ITV Merger Netflix Cuts About 1,000 Jobs; VP Film, Directors & Managers Among Affected Read More About: Comments

title: Fandango And Plex Team To Integrate Movie Ticket Sales Into Streaming
full_text: Skip to main content By Dade Hayes Dade Hayes Business Editor @dadehayes More Stories By Dade Skydance Shares Tumble In Technical Adjustment As Inflation, Interest Rate Jitters Roil Markets; Apple Regains $5 Trillion Market Cap Candle In The Wind: 5-Year-Old Media Firm Faces New Questions After Hello Sunshine Exit ‘Elsinore’ And ‘La Bola Negra’ Continue Awards Momentum With Wins At Hamptons Film Festival View All October 15, 2026 7:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source An example of the Fandango movie ticket buying feature on Plex's streaming platform Courtesy EXCLUSIVE: Established streaming platform Plex has teamed up with Fandango to allow U.S. users to find showtimes and buy movie tickets as they browse and watch films. Founded in 2011, Plex offers a suite of streaming options from free, ad-supported live and on-demand programming to transactional VOD. Its discovery and community efforts have enabled the company to hold its own in a streaming world dominated by Roku, Amazon and other large-scale players. It operates in more than 180 countries and has more than 42 million monthly active users. Fandango has branched out from its origins under current owner Versant, adding general-entertainment streaming and other offerings, but it remains the leading online movie ticket seller. Related Stories News Discovery+ Raises Prices In One Of Skydance's First Streaming Moves After Merger Close Sports Disney+ To Stream Super Bowl For First Time & Carry Two 'Monday Night Football' Games This Season Especially as moviegoing has rebounded after Covid, a number of streamers have looked to unite the small and big screens in various ways. Roku in 2025 added a “coming soon to theaters” feature to its user experience, but it stopped short of enabling ticket purchases. Watch on Deadline Under the partnership, which lit up this week, Plex users in the U.S. will see a Fandango ticketing option on title pages for movies that are currently playing in theaters. The feature lets them click through to Fandango to find showtimes and buy tickets. The integration also includes direct attribution through measurement firm Kochava, which promises to give studios and advertisers greater visibility into how campaigns and audience engagement translate into ticket sales. As more of streaming has shifted toward advertising over the past few years, with all major streamers except Apple TV making it a major strategic focus, there has also been an increased emphasis on outcomes. In other words, knowing how ads prompt purchase decisions is even more of a brass ring than ever. The Letterboxd-like community aspect of Plex is a key element in the partnership. More than 45 million users create watchlists, the company says, giving it an advantage in terms of content discovery in a marketplace where average viewers struggle to find films and series of interest. “Our vision is to make Plex the place where people can discover what to watch, regardless of where that content lives. Fandango lets us extend that experience to all theatrical releases in the U.S., giving fans an easy way to act once they find a movie they want to see,” Scott Olechowski, co-founder and chief product officer of Plex, said in a statement. “Plex has a unique view into what movie fans are actively considering, from what they’re searching for to what they’re watching across services,” said Jerramy Hainline, EVP of Fandango. “By connecting those discovery signals with Fandango ticketing, we’re making it easier for fans to turn that interest into a trip to the theater, while giving studios and advertisers a more direct, measurable path to ticket sales.” Zendaya Set For Alex Garland’s Untitled Science Fiction Movie At A24 Key Takeaways Including ‘Baywatch’, YouTube, Skydance & Banijay UK Gov’t “Minded To Intervene” Over $2.1B Sky-ITV Merger Netflix Cuts About 1,000 Jobs; VP Film, Directors & Managers Among Affected Read More About: Comments

title: Rita Coburn & Jeffrey Wright To Bring Their Feature Doc ‘W.E.B. Du Bois: Rebel With A Cause’ To London
full_text: Skip to main content By Zac Ntim Zac Ntim International Reporter @ZacharyNtim More Stories By Zac London’s Prince Charles Cinema Secures Future With New Long-Term Lease SXSW London Sets 2027 Festival Theme Thessaloniki: Adaptation Of Ioanna Karystiani’s ‘Swell’ Among 2026 Agora Works In Progress Titles View All October 15, 2026 6:55am Add us as a Google Preferred Source After its U.S. broadcast debut and theatrical roadshow tour, W .E.B. Du Bois: Rebel With A Cause , the new feature documentary by filmmaker Rita Coburn ( Marian Anderson: The Whole World in Her Hands ) on the life and legacy of the legendary writer W.E.B. Du Bois, is heading to the UK. Check out a trailer for the film above. The film will screen on Sunday, October 18, 2026, at the Charlotte Street Hotel in London. The screening will be followed by a conversation with Coburn and actor Jeffrey Wright , who narrates Du Bois’ work in the film. Directed, written, and produced by Coburn, W.E .B. Du Bois: Rebel With A Cause chronicles the extraordinary life and enduring legacy of Dr. William Edward Burghardt Du Bois, the scholar, historian, sociologist, author, activist, and Pan-Africanist whose work helped shape modern civil rights thought. Related Stories News Jeffrey Wright Taps His College Lacrosse Roots In Promo For PLL Championship Game On ABC News Dustin Hoffman, Juliette Binoche, Jeffrey Wright & Cinematographer Robert Richardson To Be Honored At Karlovy Vary Narrated by Viola Davis, the two-hour documentary explores Du Bois’ writing through dramatic readings by Common, Courtney B. Vance, and Wright. The readings are stitched together with rare archival footage, photographs, and historical documents. “I’m not prouder of any other piece that I’ve been a part of than I am to be a part of this,” Wright said of the film. Born in 1868, just five years after the Emancipation Proclamation, Du Bois lived through Reconstruction, Jim Crow, two World Wars, and the dawn of the modern Civil Rights Movement. The documentary follows his journey from groundbreaking academic achievement (Du Bois was the first African American to earn a Ph.D. from Harvard) to the founding of the NAACP, his international Pan-African work, and his death in Ghana in 1963, on the eve of the March on Washington. The documentary features commentary from leading historians, scholars, and cultural voices, including Raymond Arsenault, Karida Brown, Eric Foner, Henry Louis Gates Jr., Eddie S. Glaude Jr., Nikole Hannah-Jones, David Levering Lewis, and Imani Perry. Coburn’s previous documentaries include Maya Angelou: And Still I Rise and Marian Anderson: The Whole World in Her Hands . W.E .B. Du Bois: Rebel With A Cause screened on PBS in the U.S. in May and has since toured North America. title: Iranian Drama ‘Midday Meal’ Wins Busan Film Festival’s Top Prize, Qualifying for Oscar Consideration
full_text: × Skip to main content By Patrick Brzeski Plus Icon Patrick Brzeski Asia Bureau Chief View All October 15, 2026 6:50am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Majid Majidi's 'Midday Meal' BIFF Iranian director Majid Majidi’s Midday Meal won the best film prize at the Busan International Film Festival Thursday, giving the acclaimed drama about a teacher struggling to feed his pupils a route into the Oscars ’ best international feature race. Busan’s seven-member jury, led by Chinese filmmaking legend Zhang Yimou, said its decision was unanimous. Buzz around Majidi’s movie had been building on the ground in Busan all week, with many predicting — correctly — that it would take home the top prize. Accepting the honor at the Busan Cinema Center, Majidi dedicated his victory to the people of Iran and used portions of his speech to condemn the civilian toll of the U.S.-led war on his country. Related Stories Business Sky's $2.1 Billion ITV Megadeal: U.K. Government Eyes Intervention Movies The Academy's Bill Kramer and Lynette Howell Taylor to Attend Tokyo Film Festival “I would like to dedicate this prize to the brave heroes of Iran — the people of Iran, who have stood firm through all these years and are still resisting oppression,” he said. “On the very first day of this war in Iran, a school in Minab was hit, and 120 innocent students were killed. Even now, some of the bodies have not been found,” he later added. “What crime have our people committed? There is nothing except that our people want to be independent. They will stand firm until the end.” He concluded: “I wish for a world where there is no more war, full of peace, love and brotherhood. I’m praying for that future.” Midday Meal dazzled critics in Busan with its powerful, parable-like storytelling and assured visual style. The film follows Davoud Soulan (Mohammad Rahimi), a contract teacher in a remote village in southeastern Iran whose hopes of securing a permanent government job are jeopardized when a wealthy benefactor dies and the free lunches that keep his impoverished pupils coming to school disappear. Determined to save both his school and his future, Soulan resorts to increasingly desperate measures, including dangerous cross-border fuel smuggling, as his natural decency comes into conflict with his modest ambitions. The film continues Majidi’s longstanding thematic preoccupation with the moral pressures faced by people on society’s margins, as seen in earlier festival-winning works like The Color of Paradise (1999) and Baran (2001). For Midday Meal , he assembled an entirely nonprofessional cast through street casting in the region, setting their performances against the stark, otherworldly landscape of Iran’s so-called Martian Mountains. Earlier in the festival, Majidi spoke at length at a press conference about how he had nearly declined the invitation to travel to South Korea because he felt depressed and exhausted by the dire situation at home. He ultimately decided that the trip would allow him and his film to convey “some kind of small message from my people to the people of other nations and other places.” Majidi’s victory on Thursday night also gives Midday Meal an instantaneous jolt of Oscars buzz. The Busan festival introduced its main competition just last year, bringing its awards structure closer to those of Europe’s leading cinema events. Under rules introduced by the Film Academy, Busan’s best film winner can be submitted for international feature consideration without being selected by its country’s Oscar committee (Busan joins Cannes, Venice, Berlin, Sundance and Toronto on the Academy’s list of festivals whose designated awards offer such consideration). Iran has already chosen Babak Khajehpasha’s Land of Angels , a drama about children enduring the war in Gaza, as its official submission for the 99th Academy Awards. But Midday Meal now has an open, alternate route to the race. Majidi previously made Oscar history with Children of Heaven (1997), which became the first Iranian film nominated in the international category, then known as best foreign-language film. Among the other main competition winners, Indonesian director Eddie Cahyono received the special jury prize for Ibuku . The film stars veteran screen actress Christine Hakim as a widow whose late husband’s gambling debts force her to arrange a marriage for her only daughter, setting in motion an anguished mother-daughter drama. Taiwan’s Lee Yun Chan won best director for To Be Ordinary , about a family whose strained relationships are tested by a devastating accident. The award marks a return to the Busan spotlight for Lee, whose debut feature, The Shoe Fairy , screened in the festival’s New Currents section in 2005. The two best actor awards went to Chinese star Zhou Xun and Japanese newcomer Kashun Himeno. Zhou was recognized for Gu You’s The First Taste of Loneliness , which follows three generations of women navigating grief after the death of the family’s patriarch. The film also earned the artistic contribution award for Li Danfeng’s sound work. Himeno won for her screen debut in Shuichi Okita’s Satoko Always . She plays the youngest of three women who share a name but occupy different stages of life, each turning to writing to make sense of her experiences. India’s Shashank Walia earlier won the New Currents Award for Birds in the Dark , a black-and-white Punjabi-language drama exploring caste, labor and love in rural Punjab. The film, backed by filmmaker Hansal Mehta, had already collected the Songwon Vision Audience Award for an Asian title the previous evening. And a New Currents special mention went to South Korean director Lim Hayeon’s debut feature Beach Fictions , about a young woman whose escape to a seaside town brings enigmatic encounters with a novelist, a magician and a fortune teller. Zhang’s jury assessed 13 competition titles. Joining him on the panel were Chinese director Bi Gan, Korean actress Moon Choi, Japanese filmmaker Kei Ishikawa, Korean director July Jung, Vietnamese producer Tran Thi Bich Ngoc and Kazakh actress Samal Yeslyamova. Busan organizers reported total attendance at the festival of more than 200,000 moviegoers this year, the event’s biggest crowd since 2015. Other programs and special events drew an additional 77,000 attendees, they said. The festival linked the growth to changes in its opening schedule and an expanded screening program. The accompanying Asian Contents & Film Market, held Oct. 10-13, attracted 30,484 participants and 339 companies from 32 countries. In other starry moments, BIFF’s 31st edition, which ran Oct. 6-15, welcomed Alfonso Cuarón on his first visit to South Korea, alongside guests including Charlotte Gainsbourg, Maggie Gyllenhaal, Fan Bingbing, Hirokazu Koreeda, Lee Chang-dong, Na Hong-jin, Lav Diaz and anime veteran Rintaro. Michelle Yeoh received the Asian Filmmaker of the Year award at the opening ceremony, while Hong Kong director Ann Hui accepted the Camellia Award. title: Easterseals Disability Arts & Culture Awards Honor ‘The Pitt’, PBS Docuseries ‘Renegades’, ‘Facts of Life’ Trailblazer Geri Jewell & More
full_text: Skip to main content By Destiny Jackson Destiny Jackson Crafts Editor, Awards @DestinyDreadful More Stories By Destiny CAPE’s 35th Anniversary Gala Raises $350K As Randall Park, Manny Jacinto, The Women Of ‘The Pitt’ & More Celebrate BTS’ RM Explores Fame, Identity & Curiosity In Debut Art Exhibition ‘Between You And Me’ At SFMOMA Noah Hawley On His Sentimental ‘Amazing Spider-Man #1000’ Comic Book Debut: “He’s The New York Mets Of Superheroes” View All October 15, 2026 6:30am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Easterseals Disability Arts & Culture Awards Easterseals Southern California The inaugural Easterseals Disability Arts & Culture Awards ( DARCYS ) celebrated its first competitive class of winners Saturday, marking a new chapter for an awards program formerly known as the Media Access Awards, established in 1979. Co-produced by Easterseals Southern California and Film Independent, the ceremony recognized achievements in authentic disability representation across film, television and media, honoring the performers, filmmakers and storytellers working to reshape narratives in entertainment. Hosted by comedian and cerebral palsy advocate Tina Friml, the ceremony took place at The Barker Hangar in Santa Monica, combining humor with pointed calls for the film and television industry to invest more in recruiting disabled talent. Among the evening’s winners were PBS docuseries Renegades and HBO’s The Pitt , while Facts of Life star Geri Jewell received the inaugural DARCYS Legacy Award and Vincent Rutley took home the Christopher Reeve Emerging Talent Award. Related Stories Casting Casting Society Reveals Artios Awards Non-Film Nominees List: 'The Pitt', 'Heated Rivalry,' 'Pluribus' & More News CAPE's 35th Anniversary Gala Raises $350K As Randall Park, Manny Jacinto, The Women Of 'The Pitt' & More Celebrate Film Independent President Juan Devis, who took over in April this year, replacing acting president Brenda Robinson, who took over the role after the passing of Josh Welsh in January 2025, said that he was happy to continue the organization’s relationship with Easterseals, which has spanned more than a decade. “What we have been fighting for, for 42 years, is access and representation and pushing for the entire ecosystem to understand the value of what we bring,” Devis told Deadline. “Each year I think it becomes more evident that these types of events are just part of who we are.” Watch on Deadline Friml established the afternoon’s tone with an opening monologue that humorously described the gathering as a “truly mass disabling event.” Explaining the DARCYS acronym, she offered her own interpretation of the Y: “Yeah, you’re a good person for watching this.” The comedian also aimed at the healthcare industry, referencing The Pitt , one of the ceremony’s nominees. “The only way to get healthcare [these days] is by going to a fake hospital,” she said, before adding, “I’m still on a payment plan with Doc McStuffins, and that ended six years ago.” Among the biggest laughs of the ceremony came during Friml’s take on an awards-show in memoriam. Instead of honoring industry figures who had died, she eulogized disability tropes onscreen, including “Characters That Would Rather Die Than Be Disabled,” “The Miracle Cure,” “Cripping Up”—the practice of casting non-disabled actors in disabled roles—and “Teary Eyes.” On the first trope, Friml joked, “Sure, your career as a boxer may be over, but have you tried telemarketing?” For “Teary Eyes,” she delivered another punchline: “I don’t want Michael B. Jordan crying because a puppy is dead. I want him crying because a hot woman is still alive.” The humor gave way to a more urgent industry appeal when Amanda Upson, series producer of Renegades , accepted the award for Best Unscripted Series. The five-episode PBS short-film docuseries, hosted by award-winning musician and disability rights advocate Lachi, highlights the lives and cultural contributions of lesser-known historical figures with disabilities. Upson said the project grew into a vision shared by more than 50 disabled filmmakers, emphasizing the value of employing disabled talent both behind and in front of the camera.“We prove that empowering disabled talent behind the camera yields nuanced storytelling that outperforms traditional programming. Please check out their work and hire them,” she said. Upson also called on studios, streamers and foundations to provide more funding for disabled creators, citing approximately $45 million in funding cuts under the current administration and warning of the consequences for disabled artists and their ability to tell their stories. “In the face of near-invisible onscreen representation in this onslaught of systematic erasure, we need allies,” she said. “Studios and foundations, it is your turn to show up and invest mightily in us.” The Pitt won Best Scripted Series and Best Achievement in a Casting Ensemble, with cast members and casting director Cathy Sandrich using their acceptance speeches to highlight the importance of authentic representation. Tal Anderson, who appeared alongside fellow cast members Taylor Dearden, Jessica “Limer” Flores, Christopher Thornton and Diana Elizabeth Jordan, thanked Easterseals, HBO Max and Warner Bros. before recognizing the work of the series’ cast and crew. “Authentic representation is very, very important,” Anderson said. “And The Pitt has done such an amazing, spectacular job when it comes to authentic stories and representation.” Sandrich, accepting on behalf of the casting team, credited creators John Wells, R. Scott Gemmill and Noah Wyle with a commitment to telling stories that reflect the world and communities that have too often been underrepresented on television. “It was an enormous thrill for all of us to cast a disabled actor in a role that had not originally been conceived or written as a character with a disability,” she said. Sandrich also spoke about the importance of audiences seeing themselves reflected on screen, saying that the series’ commitment to authentic casting extended to changing a character’s gender to get the casting right. She praised the performances of Anderson, Thornton and Flores, and noted that the writers had also created roles specifically for disabled actors.“Their talents are undeniable,” Sandrich said. “We feel incredibly lucky to be given such extraordinary material, and we know that our writers, producers, and directors will continue their commitment to reflecting the truth and complexity of our world.” Rutley, recipient of the Christopher Reeve Emerging Talent Award, noted that the ceremony fell on his 41st birthday and offered encouragement to actors still waiting for their breakthrough. “I want to say today is my 41st birthday and I want to give a shout-out to all of the actors whose career didn’t blow up until after 40. I’ll see you on set,” he said. “It’s not a matter of if. It’s a matter of when. Your number will be called. Your name will be called. Today is my day. Tomorrow may be yours. Let’s ride. Love you.” Jewell, meanwhile, reflected on her career and the support of Norman Lear, who cast her in The Facts of Life after seeing her stand-up comedy routine. Jewell recalled meeting Lear in 1980 at the second annual Media Access Awards, where her friend, producer Fern Field, introduced them. “He said, ‘You’re real funny, kid, but you’re way before your time.’ I said, ‘So wait a couple months.’ He waited two months, and then he cast me on The Facts of Life ,” Jewell said. Accepting the Legacy Award at age 70, the comedian reflected on the significance of the recognition and encouraged others to believe in themselves. “I just want to say believe in yourself always, no matter what anybody else believes about you, because anybody who has believed negative confidence or what they think you can’t do, that’s not going to carry you in life. What’s going to kill you is what you believe about yourself, and never underestimate the power of the human spirit. Thank you, and God bless you.” Among those in attendance were Marlee Matlin, Wendi McLendon-Covey, Lisa Whelchel, John Ortiz, Marissa Bode, Cesily Collette Taylor, Scoot McNairy, Abby Elliott, Karen Pittman, Jamie Brewer, Victoria Mack, Daniel Monks, Jessy Yates, Matthew Reeve, Devis and Lynell Davis of Easterseals Southern California. title: Sky’s $2.1 Billion ITV Megadeal: U.K. Government Eyes Intervention
full_text: × Skip to main content By Georg Szalai Plus Icon Georg Szalai Global Business Editor View All October 15, 2026 6:10am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Secretary of State for Culture, Media and Sport Lisa Nandy on her way to a weekly cabinet meeting at 10 Downing Street earlier this year. Peter Nicholls/Getty Images The U.K. government is “minded to intervene” in the planned $2.1 billion takeover of ITV ’s TV networks and streaming assets by Comcast ‘s Sky , U.K. Culture Secretary Lisa Nandy said on Thursday. The ITV-Sky deal promises to bring together Britain’s largest pay-TV operator with its largest commercial free-to-air broadcaster. Sky CEO Dana Strong called it “ a defining moment for British media .” ITV CEO Carolyn McCall touted it as the creation of “a U.K. champion with the scale and resources to better compete with global streaming platforms.” But critics have expressed concerns about the merged entity’s market power. And now, the Labour Party government in the U.K. has also cited concentration worries. During an appearance in the London parliament, she mentioned “public interest considerations,” such as “the need for free expression of opinion in news media” and “the need for a sufficient plurality of views in news media in each market.” Nandy also highlighted “the need for the availability throughout the United Kingdom of a wide range of broadcasting, on-demand programs or both.” ITV agreed to sell its media and entertainment arm to Sky for £1.6 billion in July. The deal covers ITV’s terrestrial TV channels and streaming service ITVX. Production arm ITV Studios would continue operating as a separate company. Sky is led by CEO Dana Strong. It not only operates pay-TV and streaming businesses in the U.K., Ireland and Italy but also has been growing its telecom offerings, such as broadband and mobile phone operations. Sky also owns the production arm Sky Studios, which is led by Cécile Frot-Coutaz and has been growing its investment in original content creation. Recent Sky Studios productions have included the likes of Mary & George , starring Julianne Moore; The Tattooist of Auschwitz , starring Harvey Keitel; and The Day of the Jackal , starring Eddie Redmayne. Comcast acquired Sky in 2018. THR

The Chosunilbo JNS/Imazins via Getty Images; Netflix Jennie is set to headline the soundtrack for Netflix ‘s upcoming animated film Steps with a new song. Netflix announced the soundtrack, which is entirely written and produced by prolific songwriter Justin Tranter, for the animated comedy adventure Thursday. Global pop star and Blackpink member Jennie will lead the soundtrack with a new track “Someone to Hold.” There will be four original songs on the album, with additional vocals from Academy Award nominee Amanda Seyfried, Rose Gray and Emei and a score by Kris Bowers. “I am so excited to join the Steps family and it was really fun making my first song for an animated film,” Jennie said in a statement. “I love how much heart and personality the characters have, and I’m so happy I got to be a little part of their world. Nandy confirmed in a statement she may intervene if she has “reasonable grounds to suspect” that public interest considerations are at play. These include the “need for free expression of opinion in news media,” “a sufficient plurality of views in news media” and “a sufficient plurality of persons with control of the media enterprises” serving a variety of areas around the U.K. (in effect, local news). Popular on Variety Sir Peter Bazalgette, former chair of ITV, told Variety earlier this year he thinks government policy is now more favourable to media consolidation because it’s the only way for public service broadcasters to survive in the current climate. “Domestic broadcasters across Europe are under considerable pressure from not just the streamers, but also from YouTube,” he said, pointing out that with broadcasters now competing with YouTube, Meta, TikTok and other platforms for video advertising, Sky and ITV jointly represents only a 20 to 30% market share. Bazalgette was, however, speaking under former Prime Minister Keir Starmer’s administration. While Starmer’s government was understood to be more pragmatic about M&A activity, it remains to be seen whether his replacement Andy Burnham feels the same. Although, notably, Nandy — who’d previously said she was “minded to intervene” on Skydance’s acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery — ultimately let the deal go through , just a few weeks into Burnham’s premiership. If Nandy does go ahead and issue an intervention notice to Sky and ITV, the Competition and Markets Authority as well as the media regulator Ofcom would need to assess the deal and its impact and report back to the minister. The CMA would then carry out a more detailed investigation. Nandy said she has written to Sky and ITV to inform them of her intention to further scrutinize the process. title: London’s Prince Charles Cinema Secures Future With New Long-Term Lease
full_text: Skip to main content By Zac Ntim Zac Ntim International Reporter @ZacharyNtim More Stories By Zac London’s Prince Charles Cinema Secures Future With New Long-Term Lease SXSW London Sets 2027 Festival Theme Thessaloniki: Adaptation Of Ioanna Karystiani’s ‘Swell’ Among 2026 Agora Works In Progress Titles View All October 15, 2026 5:34am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Prince Charles Cinema Tim Whitby/Getty Images for Universal Pictures. The Prince Charles Cinema (PCC) in London’s West End has signed a new long-term lease with its landlord, securing the popular venue’s future and ending an almost two-year public campaign to save the cinema. The cinema’s management team have signed a new 25-year lease with landlord Zedwell LSQ Ltd. The lease includes a no-break clause. This means both the landlord and tenant (The PCC) are locked in for the duration of the lease. Inclusion of the clause is a win for The PCC management, which had voiced concerns that Zedwell might have ambitions to shut the cinema and redevelop the site to open a more profitable business. To the Soho Society, who recommended that Westminster Council officially designate us an Asset of Community Value, and the Council, who did so… We are so incredibly thankful to each and every one of you.” Read The PCC’s full statement below. The campaign to save The PCC began in early 2025, when the cinema’s management released a public statement stating the cinema was under “serious threat” of closure. The cinema’s long-standing lease with Zedwell had been set to expire in September 2025. Under UK law, the cinema’s management team was legally entitled to a new lease. They applied for a new lease of a minimum of 15 years at the going market rent and on similar terms to their existing lease. Zedwell responded by asking to include a redevelopment break clause in the new lease that would entitle them to terminate the lease at 6 months’ notice at any time once the new lease has commenced. The PCC is the only independent cinema in the West End. The venue is popular with hipsters and young film fans. It is best known for its all-night screening events and rep seasons, which have frequently highlighted filmmakers like Paul Thomas Anderson and Stanley Kubrick. title: Russell Brand Trial: Woman Details Alleged Rape After Asking Her to Take Photos of Him Half-Naked
full_text: Oct 15, 2026 5:07am PT Russell Brand Trial: Woman Details Alleged Rape After Asking Her to Take Photos of Him Half-Naked By Ellise Shafer Plus Icon Ellise Shafer Latest Christy Carlson Romano Says Her Salary Was Half of Shia LaBeouf’s on ‘Even Stevens’: ‘We Were Co-Leads and Had the Same Screen Time’ 2 hours ago ‘Clayface’ First Reactions Praise DC Body Horror as ‘Freakishly Awesome’ and ‘Loaded With Brutal Scenes’ 1 day ago Aaron Sorkin Thinks About Reviving ‘The West Wing’ for a ‘Couple of Seconds Every Day’: ‘I Miss It’ 1 day ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source PA Images via Getty Images The second day of Russell Brand ‘s criminal trial is underway in London, with the first complainant detailing an alleged rape at the 1999 Labour Party conference in Bournemouth. Arriving to Southwark Crown Court on Thursday, Brand sported a grey suit, white shirt and black-and-white polka dot tie, with his hair tied back in a half-up bun. His wife Laura Gallacher, who has been by his side for the first two days of the trial, was not present. Related Stories Russell Brand Was 'Ruthless and Calculated' With a 'Voracious' Desire for 'Sexual Contact,' Prosecution Alleges in Rape Trial Opening Statement Russell Brand Trial: Woman Details Alleged Rape After Asking Her to Take Photos of Him Half-Naked The jury, consisting of eight men and four women, was shown video of the first complainant’s police interview, according to Sky News . She alleges that Brand raped her in her hotel room at the Labour Party conference in 1999. “I second-guessed myself if it was rape because it was so normal,” she said in the video. “Sorry… he raped me basically — I know that happened.” Popular on Variety The woman said Channel 4’s 2023 “Dispatches” documentary, in which allegations against Brand were first brought to light, “triggered” her to go to the police. At the start of the proceedings on Thursday, Sky News reported judge Mr Justice Bennathan told the jury that the allegations in the documentary have “never been tested in any court,” but it is relevant to the case since it spurred many of the alleged victims to come forward. He said the defense may suggest that the documentary caused the complainants to “twist” their memory of events, and said he thinks the doc is “one-sided and dramatic in manner,” so it will not be shown to the jury. In the police interview video, the woman said that she met Brand at a cabaret event he was performing in at the Labour Party conference. Brand was “gentlemanly” at first and she thought he was gay, saying: “It didn’t feel like he was trying it on with me.” She suggested that they go back to her hotel room to continue their conversation. Once there, she went to the toilet and emerged to find Brand half-naked and “prancing” around the room “like an ostrich,” she said. He forced her to take photos of him, she alleged — at which point she became “frightened” — and then pushed her onto the bed and took off her clothes. She tried to push him off, she said, but he was “really heavy.” She then “drifted out of her head … but I know I said no,” the woman said. “I was frightened. I remember feeling ‘what on earth have I got myself into’ — and then he did rape me,” the woman alleged as she became tearful, according to Sky News. Afterwards, she claimed that Brand behaved like nothing was wrong and left her his email address. She didn’t tell anyone about the alleged rape out of shame, she said, until she told a friend in 2023. It was her friend who first reported the incident before the alleged victim came forward to the police herself. On Wednesday, the prosecution laid out its opening statement , alleging that Brand was “ruthless and calculated” and a “sexual predator.” The actor and comedian has been charged with three counts of rape, three counts of sexual assault and one count of indecent assault relating to incidents with six women spanning from 1999 to 2009. He has pleaded not guilty and denied all allegations against him. Prosecutor Riel Karmy-Jones outlined the six claims against Brand in her opening statement. The first woman alleged that Brand raped her in her hotel room at the Labour Party conference in Bournemouth in 1999. The second alleged incident involves a woman who was working at MTV in 2001, where she claims Brand grabbed her and tried to pull her into a toilet. The third woman alleges that Brand squeezed her breasts at a party in Soho in 2004 and then orally raped her in a toilet. The fourth allegation occurred at Capital Radio in 2004/2005, where Brand allegedly pushed a woman against a wall and “aggressively” kissed her while grabbing “her body, at her breasts, sides and buttocks,” the prosecution said. The fifth woman alleges that Brand anally raped her in 2009 after they had consensual vaginal sex. The sixth claim comes from a woman who alleges Brand demanded a massage from her while she was on a work assignment in 2009. Several of the allegations received the same response from Brand when he was questioned about them by the police, the prosecution claimed. “He set out that he has never engaged in non-consensual sexual activity, and that any accounts had been reinvented or imagined after a defamatory documentary and subsequent press reporting,” Karmy-Jones said. In 2023, Brand was the subject of a joint investigation by The Sunday Times of London and Channel 4 documentary “Dispatches,” which published allegations against him of rape, sexual assault and emotional abuse. Brand strongly denied the allegations. The Metropolitan Police then began their own investigation into him, with the Crown Prosecution Service formally bringing charges against him in April and December of last year. Brand’s trial is expected to last six weeks. title: Russell Brand Trial: Woman Alleges She Was Raped By Star In Hotel Room After He Posed For Semi-Nude Photos

Russell Brand allegedly raped a woman in her hotel room after he asked her to take photographs of him in his underwear, a court has heard. On day four of Brand’s rape trial at London’s Southwark Crown Court, the jury was shown a video of a 2023 police interview with an alleged victim. The woman has a lifelong right to anonymity — Deadline refers to her as Complainant 1 (C1) — though she is being named in the court proceedings. The woman was in her twenties at the time of the alleged incident. Watch on Deadline The pair struck up a conversation after he was “playful” and tugged her ponytail. The woman recalled Brand being “polite, courteous, attentive,” and “child”-like during their interaction. She assumed he was gay and said she was not physically attracted to him. She went on to watch a cabaret event in which Brand was performing, and after the show, she suggested he come back to her hotel room as she did not wish to go to a bar or club. “He was very gentlemanly… I didn’t think he was trying it on with me,” she said. Once back at the hotel, the woman said she remembered going to the toilet and returning to find Brand in a pair of briefs, “prancing around being silly.” The woman alleged that Brand asked her to take photos of him, during which she claimed he became visibly aroused. “I could see he was getting hard,” she said during the police interview played in court. C1 claimed Brand pushed her on the bed, pulled down her trousers and underwear, and proceeded to rape her. The woman repeatedly told police that she remembered his weight on her and that he attempted to put his fingers in her mouth. C1, who became visibly emotional during her 2023 interview, alleged that he was “pushing and pushing” until he ejaculated. “I know I said, ‘No,'” she told police. “I drifted out of my head.” She continued: “I wanted him to finish quickly… and get off me. He was making a lot of noises of enjoyment and saying how pretty I was.” After the alleged incident, C1 alleged that Brand told her that he gets “tested regularly” for sexually transmitted diseases. She recalled him saying he had to leave to “get back to his Mum” and that he wrote down his email address before exiting her hotel room. “He tried to kiss me as he went,” C1 said. “He made me feel so dirty. [I felt like] it was my fault,” she told detectives. “I know I was crying; I felt stupid.” C1 said she did not report the alleged incident at the time, saying she worried that she would be told by authorities, “What did you expect?,” after inviting him back to the hotel room. C1 came forward to the police after watching the 2023 Channel 4 documentary, Russell Brand: In Plain Sight . “I feel guilty coming forward now and not before,” she told detectives. Brand, a comedian and MAGA-sphere influencer, faces three counts of rape, three charges of sexual assault and one of indecent assault based on allegations made by six women . Brand has pleaded not guilty to all charges. During evidence on Wednesday, Riel Karmy-Jones, the prosecution barrister, described Brand as “charming,” “ruthless,” and “calculating” in his efforts to satisfy his hunger for sexual activity. Karmy-Jones has stressed that none of the women who came forward know each other. Brand will set out his defense later in the trial. The court was told repeatedly that Brand declined to answer questions when interviewed by police. He instead relied on a prepared statement, in which he claimed that he did not recall meeting the women and did not remember their names. He said any sexual contact was consensual. The trial continues. title: The Academy’s Bill Kramer and Lynette Howell Taylor to Attend Tokyo Film Festival
full_text: × Skip to main content By Abid Rahman Plus Icon Abid Rahman International Editor, Digital gentlemanabroad Follow Sign Up View All October 15, 2026 3:48am Add us as a Google Preferred Source From left: Bill Kramer, Lynette Howell Taylor, Meredith Shea and Hiro Matsuoka. Courtesy of the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences and the Tokyo International Film Festival A trio of Hollywood heavyweights are set to feature in panel discussions at the fast-approaching 39th Tokyo International Film Festival (TIFF). Bill Kramer , CEO of the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences ( AMPAS ) as well as the Academy’s President Lynette Howell Taylor and chief membership, impact and industry officer Meredith Shea will be in Japan for a host of events. On Oct. 28, the Kramer, Taylor and Shea will participate in a panel discussion (details below), followed by the presentation of a leadership award to Kramer and a gathering for Academy members. And on Oct. 29, Kramer will take part in a conversation with Hiro Matsuoka, President and CEO of Japanese production giant Toho. Related Stories Movies Christian Slater, Trine Dyrholm, Dree Hemingway Join Dogma25 Feature 'Incidents of Intimacy' Movies '7 Miles Out,' Starring Lucy Halliday, Tells a Coming-of-Age Story Full of Grief, Music and Friendship As well as the above named trio, the Academy will have several additional senior executives in attendance at the festival and member reception, including Amy Homma, Director and President, Academy Museum of Motion Pictures and Academy Collection; Jenny Galante, chief revenue and business development officer; and Jennifer Davidson, chief marketing, communications and content officer. The events the Academy trio are set to be involved in include: Academy in Tokyo: Festival Panel Set for Oct. 28, this panel will “offer a behind-the-scenes look at the Oscars as well as insights into the Academy’s global initiatives and membership programs. The discussion will also explore the Academy’s perspective on the current state and future of international cinema.” Speakers from AMPAS include Bill Kramer, Lynette Howell Taylor and Meredith Shea, with Takeo Hisamatsu, TIFF Festival Director, moderating. Special Award to Be Presented to Bill Kramer Following the panel discussion on Oct. 28, Kramer, making his first visit to Asia , will receive the Global Cinema Leadership Special Award in “recognition of his significant contributions to the development of the global film industry and the advancement of film culture.” Kramer is being recognized for his work since becoming Academy CEO in 2022, including his push to further diversify and globalize the Academy’s membership, and overseeing all of the Academy’s global operations and programs, including the Oscars, the Academy Foundation, and services for the organization’s 11,000 global members. Academy in Tokyo: Member Gathering The final event on Oct. 28 will be a private reception for Academy members from around the world, will take place. Members of the Academy’s global film community will come together at TIFF for an opportunity to connect and exchange ideas. Academy in Tokyo: Special Talk Session On Oct. 29, Kramer will participate in a wide-ranging dialogue with Toho President and CEO Hiro Matsuoka. The two will discuss the “global cinematic landscape, the future of theatrical and streaming distribution, and next steps for international collaboration.” THR

title: Christian Slater, Trine Dyrholm,  Dree Hemingway Join Dogma25 Feature ‘Incidents of Intimacy’
full_text: × Skip to main content By Scott Roxborough Plus Icon Scott Roxborough Europe Bureau Chief sroxborough Follow Sign Up View All October 15, 2026 2:38am Add us as a Google Preferred Source (R to L): Christian Slater, Trine Dyrholm Anders-Overgaard Christian Slater ( Mr. Robot ), Dree Hemingway ( Starlet ), and Danish star Trine Dyrholm ( Queen of Hearts ) have signed on to star in Incidents of Intimacy , from director Jasper Just. Johannes Lilleøre, Julie Agnete Vang, Laura Drasbæk and Michael Moritzen will co-star. The low-budget feature will mark Just’s directorial debut, and be the second in the new Dogma25 slate of ambitious arthouse features from producer Zentropa. Dyrholm, whose credits include Susanne Bier’s Oscar-winner In a Better World , Magnus von Horn’s The Girl With The Needle and Nikolaj Arcel’s A Royal Affair , will play Linda, an intimacy coordinator who struggles to form intimate connections. Unable to acknowledge or access her own feelings, she steals objects from people instead of getting close to them, filing her loot in an archive of intimacy in her cupboard. Related Stories General News Iranian Filmmaker Majid Majidi Denounces U.S. War as 'Midday Meal' Emerges as Busan Fest Standout Lifestyle Alan Mandell, Esteemed Actor and Interpreter of Samuel Beckett Plays, Dies at 98 The project will see Slater return to Danish cinema after co-starring Lars von Trier’s Nymphomaniac . Just is best known as a visual artist. He represented Denmark at the 2013 Venice Biennale and has presented solo exhibitions around the world. Much of his work deconstructs conventional representations of gender, love, social norms in mainstream cinema. Incidents of Intimacy will be his first feature as a director. Just co-wrote the script together with Sissel Dalsgaard Thomsen ( The Quiet Migration ). The film will be the second produced under the Dogma25 label, a slate of arthouse features to be made under a strict “vow of chastity” that requires the directors to comply with several enforced restrictions, including keeping the crew to a maximum of ten people, having at least half of the film be dialogue-free, and a ban on using the Internet for research or development. The films each have a maximum budget of 10 million Danish Krone (around $1.5 million) with backing from Zentropa, Danish public broadcaster DR, and Nordisk Film Distribution. All the movies will be released theatrically in Denmark via Nordisk Film, with Netflix taking streaming rights in the Nordics. TrustNordisk is handling world sales. Zentropa unveiled the Dogma25 concept at the Cannes Film Festival last year together with the group’s five directors: Just, May el-Toukhy ( Queen of Hearts ), Milad Alami ( Opponent ), Annika Berg ( Team Hurricane ), and Isabella Eklöf ( Kalak ). The group takes its name from the Dogme 95 movement, started by Danish directors Lars Von Trier, Thomas Vinterberg ( The Celebration ) Kristian Levring ( The King is Alive ) and Søren Kragh-Jacobsen ( Mifune ), another back-to-basics film movement that is credited with revitalizing indie cinema in the late ’90s.T The movement has already inspired a similar project in Germany , with director Tom Tykwer ( Run Lola Run ), Ilker Çatak ( The Teacher’s Lounge ), Nora Fingscheidt ( The Outrun ), Helene Hegemann ( Axolotl Overkill ) and Kurdwin Ayub ( Mond ) announcing their own Dogma 25 slate. title: ‘7 Miles Out,’ Starring Lucy Halliday, Tells a Coming-of-Age Story Full of Grief, Music and Friendship
full_text: × Skip to main content By Georg Szalai Plus Icon Georg Szalai Global Business Editor View All October 15, 2026 2:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source '7 Miles Out' film still Courtesy of BFI London Film Festival British writer-director Carol Morley ( Dreams of a Life , The Falling ) has adapted her moving semi-autobiographical novel 7 Miles Out , about her adolescence in Stockport, near Manchester, during the 1970s and 1980s, into a coming-of-age journey for the big screen. Lucy Halliday ( Blue Jean , The Testaments ) stars as Ann, who struggles with grief after the death of her beloved father, portrayed by Aidan Gillen ( Game of Thrones, Peaky Blinders, Queer as Folk ), and finds escapism in the new-wave punk movement and her friendship with Hel. Gemma Whelan ( Game of Thrones, Killing Eve ) stars as her mother in the movie, which features a soundtrack fit for the era, full of Joy Division, New Order, The Raincoats and more. 7 Miles Out is as much a story about finding one’s own voice and creativity as it is an ode to friendship. Related Stories Business CNN Targets Cord-Cutters In Canada With Streaming Launch Lifestyle Sally Rooney's Books Pulled From U.K. Shelves Amid Controversy Over Palestine Action Support When local band Joy Division’s frontman Ian Curtis kills himself, and Hel leaves town, everything collapses for Ann, who turns to alcohol and casual sex. But a rekindling of the past and a rediscovered cassette tape may provide a pathway to a new beginning. Original songs performed in the film are written by Morley and Carly Paradis, who also handled the score. The cinematographer is Morley’s frequent collaborator Agnès Godard ( The Falling, Beau Travail ), with editing by Raluca Petre. (Time) travel to England a few decades ago with a clip for the film right here. 7 Miles Out world premieres in the official competition of the LFF on Saturday. Morley talked to THR about the challenges and joys of adapting one’s own novel, finding the right person to play Ann, and why, despite suicide, grief and other darkness, 7 Miles Out also features so much joy and hope. When did you know or decide that you would adapt your book into a film? When I was making Dreams of a Life , I wrote the book because we were finding it hard to finance that film, and I got quite frustrated. So I wrote the book, and I felt it was complete – in the sense of putting that away after having looked at that part of my life and made something creative out of it. During COVID, Michael Winterbottom interviewed me for a book he did about British filmmakers. And he said, “I read 7 Miles Out . You should turn it into a film.” And that made me begin to think about that possibility. How do you approach adaptations? I adapted Martin Amis’ Night Train into Out of Blue , and what I realized doing that adaptation is how much you move away from the original source. I think you have to transpose literary things for the screen. With 7 Miles Out , I did think it would be easier because it’s my own book, but it wasn’t. It was harder in a sense, and in some ways, it was easier because I just looked at other events that had occurred, so it was very authentic. But you still have to shape it into a screenplay and not have as many characters or as many episodes. You’re really trying to create a throughline. What’s beautiful, compared to a book, is that with the film you have sound and music and actual dialog. And you have actors, performances, and locations. So you’re not imagining it in the same way. In terms of my book and the film, the themes are the same, but the episodes change. I want to know what Courtesy of BFI London Film Festival Let’s talk a bit more about the themes and your take on them. Grief and community are central themes of 7 Miles Out … Yes, with grief, it’s that idea that grieving isn’t instantaneous. I don’t think you get over it. You incorporate it into your life. So I really wanted to make a film where tragedy and grieving were not something that you get over, but something that you live with. It can make you think more deeply about the world and lead to creative actions, like the music in the film. I really wanted to look at it in a way that was much more complex, possibly, than it is looked at in other places. And in terms of community, I remember early on, I was really interested in looking at different generations as well. Young people’s tendency is to think about themselves as the center of the world. But they’re surrounded by these other people that they relate to. So it’s about that sense of community in a small town as well. Yes, the film feels like a smaller version of the bigger universe… Yes, it’s like a microcosm of the world, and what goes on within this community is reflecting the larger world. How did you think about mixing the darker sides with the lighter sides and hope? I often look at quite dark subject matters. For example, Dreams of a Life is about a woman that lay dead in her flat for three years. And I remember people at the time saying it was awfully optimistic. I felt oddly happy, and they couldn’t understand why. I think they thought it would be grim only. But it celebrated a life. And it also made people think about friendship and how they could make a difference in the world. With 7 Miles Out , I wanted people to feel the light at the end. The film particularly talks about suicide, which was very taboo back then. Even now it’s very hard to talk about. So I wanted to make a film that addressed that. Suicide is one of the biggest causes of death of young men under 50 globally. So I wanted to look at suicide in a way that people afterwards could talk about, but not feel completely disempowered. The young woman in the film making music and writing songs and becoming able to express herself in a different way was, to be very obvious, about her finding her voice, which was very important. Rather than you feeling very down at the end, I hope that you feel like you’ve been through a lot of emotions, and at the end you feel lighter and enlightened, and you feel like you can go and process some of your own feelings. It was more about catharsis. Carol Morley, courtesy of Paul Marc Mitchell 7 Miles Out is based on my dad and his suicide. When I was growing up and when he saw a psychiatrist, he would be okay because he could present himself. In my research into suicide, [I found] that people who are going to kill themselves often make that decision a few weeks before, and they start to seem happy because they have resolved something. So people go, “I saw him the day before, and he seemed happy, so I couldn’t believe it.” That’s why I think I make films about the idea of what people represent to the world and who they really are inside, which you cannot always tell. How did you find your amazing cast? I cast with casting director Shaheen Baig, and we decided to do a massive open casting call in Stockport, and 450 people came to that. With the younger cast, they sent videos. A lot of the cast are first-timers. They’ve never done anything, and I find that enormously exciting. I’d seen Lucy Halliday in Blue Jean . We did a Zoom interview because she was filming in Canada, and we really got on. But for me, it’s all about meeting them. So we met at Shaheen’s offices and spoke for about two hours. Shaheen came in at one point and went, “Is everything all right?” I just felt this energy she had and ability to just [express various layers]. So, as soon as I met her, she was Ann for me. Aidan, I actually had briefly once, and [at another event,] I went over to him and said: “I met you once. Would you be in a film for 10 minutes?” I said we’d send the script to his agent. And then his friend got in touch and said, “Aidan wants to be in touch.” So I ended up meeting Aidan the next week, and he had read it and wanted to be in. Aidan had a conversation with my brother, and my brother afterwards said that was the best conversation he’d ever had in his life. Aidan wanted to talk to my brother about my dad because my brother’s nine years older than me, so Aidan really wanted that perspective, And weirdly, with Gemma Whelan, what I found out was that the very first thing she did was my short film The Madness of the Dance [in which she appeared as a nun]. So, I keep going: “I discovered you.” And she goes: “I launched you.” So, we had the core of the cast. And then Kasper Hilton-Hille ( Peaky Blinders: The Immortal Man , Outrageous ) is brilliant as Ann’s brother. ‘7 Miles Out,’ courtesy of BFI London Film Festival Where did you film, and were any scenes particularly difficult to shoot? We were on a very stringent budget, so I knew I couldn’t ever do reshoots or pick-ups. I had to get it all at the time. So if it rained, we were filming in the rain. Now, rain never shows up as much on film as it really is. So the filming in the rain was really hard because you’re having to protect the equipment, and the actors are just getting more drenched than they look. We filmed everything within a 15-minute radius in Stockport. Agnès Godard had never been to Stockport, so I love that. She was seeing it through a different lens, and so the combination of us was good. I love working with Agnès. She calls me “dangerous girl” because I like to be in the moment. I have a plan, but change it at the last minute if I notice something. And all the songs that you see people sing are all sung live. I wanted that live feeling, which was very challenging but we did a lot of prep. None of those girls could play. Leila [Entwistle who plays Hel] picked up the bass and looked like she could play it. And she did because it was quite simple as the punk idea was that anyone can play. And they all went for it. 7 Miles Out is set in a very specific time and location but feels like people in other parts of the world will quite easily connect with the core themes and emotions. What do you think? A filmmaker said you could make a film about a village that’s universal. If you make a film where you are primarily conveying emotion, that will connect with everybody. I’m personally not interested in nostalgia. I’m interested in authenticity. So it’s really a great thing to look at things that have happened to you personally to draw out that authenticity. When I made a film a long time ago called The Alcohol Years , which was a documentary about Manchester, I discovered people in Melbourne and America were writing. People in Australia said it was just like Melbourne, and people from the U.S. said it was just like New York. I think that music has that ability to really transcend place. Do you know what you will do next? I really want to work within a genre I’ve not worked in yet. I definitely have got something in mind that would be cross-generational, working with young people and old people, set in a time I’ve never worked in before and a place I’ve never worked in before. I never want to repeat myself. THR
